newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters sparks selloff in New Zealand dlr at close.
newsitem.headline: Peters sparks selloff in New Zealand dlr at close.

text.p: Comments from Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday sparked a sell off in the New Zealand dollar.
Dealers said the Kiwi was vulnerable to further selling if offshore players "misread" Peters' comments but the New Zealand market was also vulnerable to a Reserve Bank comment and a sharp pullback.
The kiwi ended at 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) at US$0.6734/39 from its 0.6758/65 opening and 0.6745/52 close on Tuesday.
Peters told a news conference in Sydney that the New Zealand dollar could fall further.
"It will probably go a bit further still on forecasts," he said.
Dealers said his comments were innocuous enough. "But it was like a red rag to a bull for the market," said one, "and if people offshore see that they may react."
But with the Monetary Conditions Index dropping sharply to 60 basis points below the Reserve Bank's desired level, interest rates were likely to rise and that should see the kiwi also retrace.
Against that, dealers said the kiwi was hovering just above important support and stops at 0.6730, and if those bust then it could sink quickly.
"If those are triggered then we are in danger of triggering a comment from the Reserve Bank," a dealer said.
The market will also be focusing on March quarter Balance of Payments data on Friday and in its current mood could sell off if the data is worse than expected.
